Important Notice:

As required by regulatory guidance issued by the Insurance Authority, certain insurance product names have been updated to include the word “insurance” and more clearly reflect its nature as an insurance product. This is a naming change only and does not affect the benefits, terms and conditions, or coverage of the policies.

Beware of scams! Please do not provide any bank, credit card, investment, insurance, MPF account or other important personal information like your login ID and password via phone numbers or hyperlinks embedded in suspicious messages purporting to be from CTF Life.

We would like to take this opportunity to remind customers that we will only send SMS using Registered SMS Sender ID with prefix #CTFLife. If there any doubts regarding the legitimacy of the messages received or the sender, please contact CTF Life Hotline (852) 2866 8898. If you suspect you have been scammed, please report to the police or call the Anti-Scam Helpline of Anti-Deception Coordination Centre on 18222 immediately.

Policyholder Dividend and Crediting Interest Philosophy

Applicable to All Participating Policies

  1. We issue participating life policies, which offer the Policyholders with non-guaranteed dividends/bonuses including annual dividends, reversionary bonuses, terminal dividends and/or terminal bonuses. Annual dividends and reversionary bonuses are generally declared per annum, while terminal dividends and terminal bonuses are generally payable upon policy surrender, death of Insured or policy maturity.
  2. Premium income received from the Policyholder is invested in an investment portfolio to support the participating Product Group. Through the policy dividends/bonuses declaration, the policyholders participate in the financial performance of the Product Group. Financial performance may be affected by both past experience and future outlook for all the factors including, but not limited to, investment performance of the underlying asset supporting the Product Group, expenses, persistency, and claims. The experience over the long-term is compared against expectation, and the non-guaranteed dividends/bonuses are adjusted if the experience over the long-term is different from the expectation.
  3. Due to the variation of features and benefits of different products, the frequency and magnitude for the change in dividend/bonus may vary for different products. In general, the adjustments on dividends/bonuses are more frequent and significant for products with higher risk profile. Policies of the same product may be separated into different bucket with different dividend/bonus, with an aim to more closely reflect the underlying financial performance.
  4. To stabilize the dividend/bonus, we may distribute a proportion of the financial performance in a particular year attributable to the Policyholder, with an aim to smooth out the short-term volatility of dividend/bonus over the course of the policy term. When future investment performance is worse than expected, the company’s shareholder may share less from the investment performance such that more may be allocated for dividend payment/bonus distribution, and vice versa.
  5. The Board, having regard to the advice of the Appointed Actuary and reviewed by Risk and Investment Committee which must include one independent non-executive director, will review and determine the dividend/bonus at least once per year. The declared dividend/bonus may be different from those illustrated in the relevant product information provided, e.g. benefit illustrations. In case of any change in the actual dividend/bonus against the illustration or should there be a change in the projected future dividend, such change will be reflected in the policy anniversary statement and an updated Basic Plan Benefit Summary.

Applicable to All Universal Life policies

  1. We issue universal life policies, which credit the Policyholders’ account with interest that is not guaranteed.
  2. Premium income received from the Policyholder is invested in an investment portfolio to support the product. Through the crediting interest rate declaration that allows for the profit target of the Company and minimum guaranteed crediting interest rate, the Policyholder participates in the investment performance of the portfolio. The crediting interest rate declaration may be affected by both past experience and future outlook for all the factors including, but not limited to, market conditions, investment outlook, persistency and claims.
  3. Due to the variation of features and benefits of different products, the frequency and magnitude for the change in crediting interest rate may vary for the different products. In general, the adjustments on crediting interest rate scale are more frequent and significant for products with higher risk profile.
  4. To stabilize the crediting interest rate, we may distribute a proportion of the investment income in a particular year attributable to the Policyholder, with an aim to smooth out the short-term volatility of crediting interest rate over the course of policy term.
  5. The Board, having regard to the advice of the Appointed Actuary and reviewed by Risk and Investment Committee which must include one independent non-executive director, will review and determine the crediting interest rate at least once per year. The declared crediting interest rate may be different from those illustrated in the relevant product information provided, e.g. benefit illustrations. In case of any change in the actual crediting interest rate against the illustration or should there be a change in the projected future crediting interest rates, such change will be reflected in the policy anniversary statement and an updated Basic Plan Benefit Summary.
  6. The actual crediting interest rate will vary from time to time and will be subject to a minimum level if the product offers a guaranteed interest rate.

Investment Philosophy, Policy and Strategy

Applicable to All Participating Policies and Universal Life Policies

  1. Our investment philosophy is to deliver long-term stable return which is in line with the product and the Company’s business and financial objectives.
  2. Our investment policy aims to achieve the targeted long-term investment results and reduce volatility in investment returns over time. It also aims to control and diversity risk exposures, maintaining adequate liquidity and manage the assets with respect to the product features.
  3. Investment instruments include cash, deposits, sovereign bonds, corporate bonds, listed equities, funds, private investments and/or other investment products. Derivatives and other hedging instruments may be used to manage investment risk at the Company's decision based on its long-term market view and asset-liability positions. It should be noted that residual investment risk may still exist after hedging.
  4. The asset portfolio also targets to provide diversification across different geographic regions (focus on the U.S., Europe and Asia Pacific markets) and industries to the extent the size of portfolio can support.
  5. For fixed income investment, currency exposure of the underlying policies is mitigated by closely matching either through direct investments in the same currency denomination or the use of currency hedging instruments.
  6. The asset portfolio is actively managed by investment professionals, who will also closely monitor the investment performance. The investment strategy may be subject to change depending on the investment views and economic outlook. In case of any changes in the investment strategy, we will inform our Owners for any material changes, rationale for the change and any impact to the Owners.
  7. For participating policies, our current long-term target asset allocation attributed to individual products are as follows:

Fulfillment Ratios of Dividends/Bonuses

The following are Fulfillment Ratios of non-guaranteed Annual Dividends, Reversionary Bonuses, Terminal Dividends, Terminal Bonuses and policy value for products which have new policies issued since 1 January 2010. The ratios are calculated up to the respective policy anniversary in the current reporting year.

The fulfillment ratio for annual dividends is calculated as the ratio of aggregate actual accumulated non-guaranteed annual dividends and interest at their respective policy anniversary in year 2025 against the respective illustration amounts at the point of sale for all relevant policies that were in-force in year 2025.

The fulfillment ratio for reversionary bonuses is calculated as the ratio of aggregate actual accumulated non-guaranteed reversionary bonuses at their respective policy anniversary in relevant year against the respective illustrated amounts at the point of sale for all relevant policies that were in-force in year 2025 and for all relevant policies actually terminated in 2025. For avoidance of doubt, cash value of reversionary bonuses is used in the calculation.

The fulfillment ratio for terminal dividends/bonuses is calculated as the ratio of aggregate payout of terminal dividends/bonuses against the illustrated amounts at the point of sale for all relevant policies actually terminated in 2025. Similarly, cash value of terminal bonuses is used in the calculation. For avoidance of doubt, cash value of terminal bonuses is used in the calculation.

The fulfillment ratio for policy value is calculated as the ratio of aggregate payout of policy value against the illustrated amounts at the point of sale for all relevant policies actually terminated in 2025.

For the purpose of calculation of Fulfillment Ratios, it is assumed that:

  • All annual dividends (if any) and cash coupons (if any) declared are left with the company for interest accumulation since policy issuance based on the relevant actual interest rates.
  • Premiums have been paid up to the end of policy year.
  • All guaranteed monthly incomes (if any) and non-guaranteed monthly incomes (if any) paid are left with the Company for interest accumulation since policy issuance based on the relevant actual interest rates.
  • There is no change in Sum Insured / Unit of the policy since policy issuance.
  • No policy loans are taken since policy issuance.

Fulfillment Ratios may not be applicable due to the following reason(s):

  1. No relevant policy is in-force with the respective policy year as of current reporting year(“No policy”).
  2. The amount of accumulated annual dividends and interest/reversionary bonuses illustrated at the point of sale up to the respective policy year as of current reporting year is zero for the relevant policies(“Zero bonus”).
  3. No terminal dividends/bonuses or policy value was paid in reporting year:

    • No terminal dividends/bonuses or policy value was entitled by the policy upon the termination of the policy in the respective policy year(“Zero bonus”); and/or
    • No relevant policy was actually terminated in the respective policy year(“No termination”).
Please be reminded that the annual dividends, reversionary bonuses, terminal dividends/bonuses and policy value history is not an indicator of future performance of our participating products.

Total Cash Value Ratio

The following are total cash value ratios for products which have new policies issued since 1 January 2010. The total cash value ratios are calculated up to the respective policy anniversary in the current reporting year.

The total cash value ratio is calculated as the ratio of aggregate actual total cash values at their respective policy anniversary in year 2025 against the respective illustration amounts at the point of sale for all relevant policies that were in-force in year 2025. Total cash value includes both guaranteed benefits (cash value, cash coupons) and non-guaranteed benefits (policy value, interest of cash coupons, annual dividends and interest/cash value of reversionary bonuses, terminal dividends/cash value of terminal bonuses).

Some of the non-guaranteed benefits (for example the policy value, terminal dividends/cash value of terminal bonuses) are only available upon termination of policy. Before a policy is actually terminated, this amount is still not guaranteed, and we have the right to increase or decrease the amount subsequently from time to time at our discretion. When we calculate the total cash value ratio, we include only policies that have not been terminated and hence the total cash value in the calculation has not been paid.

For the purpose of calculation of total cash value ratios, it is assumed that:

  • All annual dividends (if any) and cash coupons (if any) declared are left with the company for interest accumulation since policy issuance based on the relevant actual interest rates.
  • Premiums have been paid up to the end of policy year.
  • All guaranteed monthly incomes (if any) and non-guaranteed monthly incomes (if any) paid are left with the Company for interest accumulation since policy issuance based on the relevant actual interest rates.
  • There is no change in Sum Insured / Unit of the policy since policy issuance.
  • No policy loans are taken since policy issuance.

Total cash value ratios may not be applicable due to the following reason(s):

  1. No relevant policy is in-force with the respective policy year as of current reporting year(“No policy”).
  2. The amount of non-guaranteed benefits (policy value, interest of cash coupons, annual dividends and interest/cash value of reversionary bonuses, terminal dividends/cash value of terminal bonuses) illustrated at the point of sale up to the respective policy year as of current reporting year is zero for the relevant policies(“Zero bonus”).
Please be reminded that the total cash value history is not an indicator of future performance of our participating products.

Premium Levy

From 1 January 2018, the Insurance Authority (IA) will start collecting a premium levy from policy holders in accordance with the law. The levy rate will start at 0.04% of the insurance premium per policy year and increase gradually to 0.1%. The amount of the levy imposed on each policy will be subject to a cap.

Policy holders of all new or in-force life insurance policies must pay the levy along with their premium payment. The IA will collect the levy from policy holders via the insurance companies, including CTF Life.

In Phase 1 (1 January 2018 to 31 March 2019), for life insurance policies with single or annualised premiums at or above HK$100,000, policy holders will pay only HK$40 at most per policy year. Details of the levy rates and caps are set out below:

Phase 1 Phase 2 Phase 3 Phase 4
1 January 2018 to
31 March 2019 		1 April 2019 to
31 March 2020		 1 April 2020 to
31 March 2021		 1 April 2021 onwards
Levy rate 0.04% 0.06% 0.085% 0.1%
Premium levy cap
Life insurance $40 $60 $85 $100
Please note that if the currency of the policy is not arranged in HK dollars (e.g, US dollar or RMB), the premium levy will be also collected according to the policy currency.

For details of premium levy, please refer to our FAQ which has been posted in our website or you can contact our Customer Service Hotline at 2866-8898 for enquiries.

Naming Requirements for Insurance Products

Pursuant to the Insurance Authority's circular on Naming Requirements for Insurance Products, certain insurance product names will be revised to include the word "insurance" such that more clearly reflect its nature as an insurance product. The changes relate to product naming only and do not affect the coverage, benefits, terms and conditions of the in-scope policies.

Concerned policyholders are advised to take note of this update which will take effective from 1 January 2027, and relevant changes will be implemented gradually before 1 January 2027.

For details of the naming requirements, please visit [Circular on the Naming Requirements for Insurance Products].
